caption: The red peg p belongs to two overlapping domains on one two-dimensional ground surface. The right panels are flat coordinate images on the surveyors’ boards, with different scales, origins and axis choices. The dotted connections identify records of the same point; they are not a journey or a flattening of the ground. The picture is schematic and supplies no distance-preserving map.
alt: A curved terrain patch has overlapping blue and gold chart domains sharing a red peg. Two flat numerical grids, one rectangular and one oblique, label that peg with different coordinate pairs.

caption: A coordinate picture of the nonzero differential dT at p, with components (2, −1) K/m. The blue velocity (0.5, 0.2) m/s gives 0.8 K/s, while the gold velocity (0.3, 0.6) m/s lies in its kernel and gives zero. Straight contours represent the local first-order model, not all finite terrain contours. The drawing assumes no physical orthogonality or metric gradient.
alt: Parallel first-order temperature contours pass through a point p. A blue velocity crosses towards increasing temperature and yields a positive rate; a gold velocity follows the contour through p and yields zero. A panel gives the component values and readouts.
